name: Inline cable coupler
summary: A connector joining two cables without either half being mounted on equipment, such as an extension lead coupling.
description: An inline coupler joins two free cables, with neither half fixed to a panel or device. Typical uses are extension leads, portable equipment feeds and sensor cables with a disconnect point partway along the run. Drawings show both halves floating on the cable line, sometimes with a note that the coupling is located in a particular area.

Because the coupler is free, its location is not fixed by the equipment, so the drawing should state where it is. The symbol does not show ingress protection, latching or whether the coupling may be separated under load. For power couplers, the live side should be the socket half so exposed pins are not energised.
readingNotes: Identify which side is energised and confirm it is the socket half.
Look for a location note for the coupler.
drawingChecklist: Show which half is on the supply side.
Locate the coupler on the layout.
distinction: An inline coupler joins two free cables; a panel plug and socket has one half fixed to equipment.
